It’s no secret that my time in medicine almost killed me. - And I think the biggest reason why (more than the hours and the exhaustion) was this idea that we’re supposed to accept all of it with a smile. With gratitude. As if the system is doing us a FAVOUR. The 14-hour shifts, 7 days in a row. The mental overwhelm from having urgent 7 tasks competing for your attention. The constant anxiety and fear of making the wrong mistake that could cost a life. The superiors who look straight through you. And then, when you say anything about it, you’re met with: “Oh but how LUCKY are you to be a doctor?” “You’re saving lives, why would you want to do anything else?” That’s the part that really f*cking broke me 😞 I ended up leaving medicine because I just couldn’t take it any longer. And even then, I felt so guilty because of this exact attitude. I thought I was weak, for choosing not to suffer for such a prestigious career. But now that I’ve built a career that I genuinely LOVE and ENJOY every single day… I’ve learnt that suffering SHOULDN’T be a rite of passage. It’s not what makes you a good doctor. It’s not what makes you “worthy” of the title. And it was NEVER supposed to be the price you pay for a career that you love. The more that we say this out loud, and support others who are brave enough to say it too, the louder that calling gets. So, are you with me? 🙏🏽 - P.S. Bye, Darling. No more @Charlotte Tilbury for the cruelty-free community.  THE TEA: Charlotte Tilbury has now publicly announced on their website they will not be renewing their Cruelty Free International certification.  THE BACKSTORY: Cruelty Free International (previously also referred to as The Leaping Bunny Programme) is the international coalition partner to Leaping Bunny (who certified North America). They recently announced a rebrand with a new logo. Both programs remain coalition partners with the same rigorous program, just certifying different regions.  THE WHY:  Allegedly, they are concerned about the public perception of this rebrand and its potential to cause confusion  THE ISSUE: 1. Charlotte Tilbury never has to print the rebranded logo on their packaging if they find the new logo from the previous bunny confusing. If they can write the giant chunk of text as their cruelty-free policy they recently revised, then they could have just as easily explained the rebrand and continued commitment.  2. Charlotte Tilbury now claims to be cruelty-free with zero audits, annual renewals, and is left unchecked selling on China where the brand could potentially begin selling their special use goods (which are subject to animal testing) in China. We are just expected to trust them.  3. Charlotte Tilbury is owned by parent company Puig with a large portfolio of other major brands all subject to animal testing as well. CT was the only cruelty-free brand in their collection. It makes this move extra questionable.
